status_note: `levenshtein`: filed [#25113](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/25113), closed 2026-10-28 as fixed on main by [#27619](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27619) and backported to v2.0-cyanoptera; 2.0.0, the latest release, still counts bytes. `reverse`: not a bug, it reverses grapheme clusters on purpose.
summary: `levenshtein` counts bytes, not code points, on non-ASCII text, and `reverse` works on grapheme clusters. Possibly intended: check the docs before filing.
handling: sverify raises "non-ASCII text differs between engines" for these on non-ASCII text (#195, `Dialect.ascii_only`). The guard stays after the fix: Lean's evaluator follows Rust's strings and does not evaluate these functions on non-ASCII text (`core/Sverify/Core/Text.lean`), so the guard is the reference's limit, not DuckDB's workaround alone.

checked.note: reverse pass: levenshtein's DP runs over bytes (extension/core_functions/scalar/string/levenshtein.cpp#L15-L60), reverse over grapheme clusters (extension/core_functions/scalar/string/reverse.cpp#L24-L29); the text docs say 'single-character edits'; no upstream test covers either on non-ASCII text
